Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
SPECULUM, NASAL, KILLIAN'S PATTERN 



CO 



o 

z 






1. Scope — Specifies dimensions, materials and other requirements for Killian nasal speculum 
used in ENT surgery for diagnostic purposes. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1. 

2.1 Tolerances on various dimensions shall be permitted as given below: 

a) ih 0*1 mm on dimensions up to 50 mm, 

b) ± 0'2 mm on dimensions above 50 mm and up to 200 mm, 

c) ± 1*0 mm on dimensions above 200 mm and up to 500 mm, and 

d) ± 2*0 mm on dimensions above 500 mm. 

2.2 Tolerance on angular dimension shall be ± 2*". 

3. IWaterial 

3.1 The arms of the speculum including the blades shall be made of stainless steel conforming to 
designation 30Cr13 of IS : 6603-1972 * Specification for stainless steel bars and flats '. 

3.2 The material for the screw shall be the same as that for the arms of the speculum. 

3.3 The spring shall be made of stainless steel conforming to designation 30Cr13 of 15:6911-1971 
' Specification for stainless steel plate, sheet and strip '. 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The speculum shall be free from scales, pits, burrs, cracks, tool marks and other surface 
defects. 

4.2 All edges shall be smoothly rounded off. 

4.3 The joint shall be of the screw type as shown in Fig. 1, 

4.4 The adjustment screw shall function satisfactorily and when fixed at any desired position, the 
blade shall not have a play of more than 0*5 mm when measured at the tip and the blade shall not 
have a tendency to slip. The screw threads shall conform to IS : 4218 ' Specification for ISO metric 
screw threads '. 

4.5 The spring action shall be smooth. 

4.6 The blades of the speculum shall be free from imperfections siVij perfectly smooth when 
inspected visually. 

4.7 The two blades of the speculum shall match with each other exactly in the fully closed position. 

4.8 The speculum shall be finished bright and passivated. The holding surface of the arms shall 
have a matt finish.

4.8.1 The speculum shall be treated in 10 percent (vjv) nitric acid solution for not less than 
30 minutes at a temperature of not less than lO^'C and not exceeding 60X. The speculum shall 
then be rinsed in water, dried in hot air and the joint lightly lubricated with a non-toxic and non< 
corrosive substance. 

5. Heat Treatment — The speculum including the spring shall be uniformly hardened and 
tempered to a hardness of 390 to 475 HV. The hardness of the screw shall be 300 to 350 HV. 

6. Tests 

6.1 Corrosion Resistance — The speculum shall be subjected to boiling and autoclaving test in 
accordance with 18:7531-1975 * Method for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance 
of stainless steel surgical instruments '. There shall be no sign of corrosion after the test. 

6.2 Test for Spring -— The spring shall be tested by pressing either arm to the extreme position and 
releasing it. On repeating this for 50 times, there shall be no permanent set observed and the 
jaws shall not gape. 

7. Marking — The speculum shall be marked legibly and indelibly with the manufacturer's name, 
initials or registered trade-mark and the words ' Stainless Steel ' on the arm. 

7.1 ISl Certification Marliing — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — Each speculum shall be wrapped in a moisture-proof paper and then packed 
individually in a cardboard carton. Alternatively, the packing may be done as agreed to between 

the purchaser and the supplier.
